notes:
I couldn't do this research. My tools hit their usage limit on my first attempt, before any of the pages loaded, and further calls were blocked. That means I didn't read any sources: not Enduring Word, Bible Hub, StudyLight, the NET Bible notes or anything else.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say, so I haven't written notes from my own knowledge. As a result, I have no verse-by-verse notes for Job 25:1–6.

When the tools are available again (please ask me to retry), I would start with these pages:

- **Traditional reading:**
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/job-25/
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/job/25-1.htm through https://biblehub.com/commentaries/job/25-6.htm (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Barnes and others)
  - The Job 25 commentaries on studylight.org and preceptaustin.org
- **Where traditions differ:**
  - Searches on monergism.com, gty.org, wesley.nnu.edu (Wesley's notes on Job 25) and desiringgod.org. Verses 4 and 6 (how anyone can be righteous before God, and calling man a "worm") are the likeliest places for Reformed, Wesleyan and Lutheran views to differ.
- **Other views:**
  - The netbible.org notes on Job 25
  - newadvent.org (the Church Fathers on Job and Gregory the Great's *Morals on Job*)
  - bibleodyssey.org, on why Bildad's last speech is so short (the "third cycle" question)
